A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GroundCUA and GroundNext. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments, controlled training-corpus comparisons and OSWorld-Verified agentic results in Tables 2–4, Figure 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original instruction-quality evaluation, training ablations, scaling results and error analyses.

M1.justification: The reported reward definition changes: v1 normalizes distance by the image-wide maximum, whereas v2 uses half the bounding-box diameter for interior predictions and explicitly specifies signed distance. Appendix C.4 also changes the binary alternative's outside-box reward from 0 to -1. The Qwen-based SFT-to-RLOO pipeline remains; these formula revisions do not establish that the models were retrained.

E1.justification: The GroundCUA application coverage, five grounding benchmarks and OSWorld-Verified tasks remain unchanged. GUIAct experimentation and the other training corpora already appear in v1. New audits and ablations examine existing data and task coverage rather than introducing another benchmark or domain.

E2.justification: FOCUS-2B is added to the ScreenSpot-Pro comparison in v2 Table 11. Existing comparator rows remain across the matched benchmark tables. Phi-Ground-7B is more specifically labeled Phi-Ground-7B-16C-DPO with identical scores; removing table citations does not remove the associated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental protocols: 100K examples per instruction subtype, a 100-instruction audit by three independent annotators using majority vote, controlled 100K/350K/700K scaling, and group-size tests with approximately 5K RL examples. Its new RL-only corpus comparison uses 10K examples, binary 0/1 rewards and two epochs. These are additional experimental settings, not documented changes to the retained main evaluations.

E4.justification: New analyses test instruction-type utility and prompt sensitivity, generated-instruction validity, reward granularity, rollout group size, RL training-corpus quality and SFT scaling. Previously qualitative RLOO-versus-GRPO observations gain numerical evidence. Appendix E also expands error analysis with distance distributions, application-specific failures and a spreadsheet localization case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or benchmark uncertainty estimates. The new error-distance histograms and majority-vote instruction audit are supplementary analyses, not uncertainty reporting for model performance.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2–4 and existing appendix score rows are unchanged, but substantial results are added: a 4% instruction-error rate, optimizer and reward comparisons, RL-only corpus results, and scaling averages of 57.2, 60.2 and 66.4. New Table 16 also reports different UI-TARS-1.5-7B values, including 75.4 on MMB-GUI versus 64.3 in retained Table 3, without reconciling the difference.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C.4 revise the mathematical definition of normalized distance to use a location-dependent reference distance and an explicit sign convention. This is a substantive local definition change, beyond notation. The RLOO derivation remains, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same dataset and model contributions, data-efficiency claims, benchmark-performance claims and agentic applicability. The additional appendix evidence supports these existing claims rather than redefining the paper's central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for instruction-mixture benefits and scaling, qualifies RL conclusions to the studied sizes and rewards, and explicitly avoids claiming inherent RLOO superiority. Appendix E replaces the earlier small-element-selection hypothesis with a broader account of domain shift, localization precision, application semantics and spatial reasoning. The standalone limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that final-model evaluation uses benchmark instructions without prefixes and identifies preliminary checkpoints used for ablations. Its reproducibility statement expands release commitments to training code, evaluation scripts and data sheets. Core hardware and SFT hyperparameters remain unchanged; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al. (2025) when discussing combined SFT/RL training and incorporates the already-cited AriaUI into the dataset comparison and related-work discussion. Several reference entries, including GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 and InternVL3, disappear despite retained comparator rows. The central positioning around expert-annotated desktop data remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained, with localized wording corrections and a conference-publication header replacing 'Preprint.' v2 expands the appendix organization, rewrites the error-analysis discussion, and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements without broadly restructuring the existing paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated tables for instruction, reward, group-size, optimizer, RL-corpus and scaling analyses, plus error-distance histograms and a reward illustration. The original error panel becomes Figures 10–11, retaining three examples and replacing the 'choose tag' example with a spreadsheet case. Existing appendix tables are reformatted to omit citations.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the retained claims through instruction-quality validation, controlled ablations, scaling evidence and more careful RL qualifications. The gain is limited by the small audit and preliminary-checkpoint studies, absent uncertainty estimates for small experimental differences, and unreconciled UI-TARS scores in new Table 16 versus retained Table 3.
